title: Iki component (iki/v1)
description: A piece of UI the plugin adds to Iki's pages: a Web Component, in one JavaScript module, that Iki runs in a sandboxed frame with no network and no access to the person's session. Iki gives it the data it shows, with the viewer's permissions, and does anything it asks for itself (ADR 0084, ADR 0117).

^x-.description: A key for tools, such as `x-acme-reviewed`: kept in the file, ignored by Iki, and dropped from the build (ADR 0293).

apiVersion.description: The spec version this manifest follows.

name.description: The component's name in snake_case. Elsewhere it is `plugin.name`.

module.description: The JavaScript module that defines the element, such as `./components/plate-map.js`: one file, with everything it needs bundled in, since the frame loads nothing else. Up to 10 MiB.

element.description: The custom element the module defines (`customElements.define`), such as `acme-plate-map`: lower case, with a hyphen.

entities.description: The many entities it shows, in the places that give it them (every slot but a tab without a `search`): their type, with its subtypes, the fields it reads of each, and the most it holds at once. It gets only those fields, beside each entity's ID, HRID, type, title, revision and project (ADR 0117).

type.description: The type of the entities it shows, with its subtypes.

fields.description: The fields it reads of each: their values are all it's given, and a refinement it asks for can name only these (and `hrid`).

limit.description: The most it holds at once, as it asks for more a page at a time. 500 if left out.

slots.description: Where it appears on Iki's pages: at most one slot of each kind, and one tab for each type.

events.description: What it tells the page, by name. `select`: entities a person picked in it, as an `iki-select` event whose `detail.entities` lists their HRIDs, so the page can act on them. `run`: an action of its plugin a person asked to run on its entity. Asking for more entities (`iki-more`), narrowing them (`iki-refine`) and opening one it was given (`iki-open`) need no declaration.

select.description: Entities of `type` a person picked in it, which the page hears of as an `iki-select` event.

type.description: The type of the entities it selects, with its subtypes.

run.description: Actions it may offer to run on the entity whose tab it is, such as the one that fills it while it's empty: an `iki-run` event whose `detail.action` names one, qualified. Iki opens its run page with the action and the entity chosen, where the person checks and starts it. Its `place.runs` lists those the person viewing it may run there now.

actions.description: The plugin's own actions, by name, each with an input that takes the tab's type.

slot.description: `entity.tab`: a tab on the page of each entity of `type`. `search.results`: another way to see the grid's results, when it shows the component's `entities` type. `project.page`: a section on each project's page, of what its `search` finds there. `person.home`: a section on each person's home, of what its `search` finds in every project they read.

type.description: For `entity.tab`: the entities whose pages show it, with their subtypes. The other slots show the component's `entities` type.

label.description: Its tab's, section's or view's name. The component's label if left out.

search.description: The entities of the component's `entities` type that fill the slot, as the search API takes them: on a tab, those its conditions find (a box's tubes: `{ field: box, op: eq, value: "{{ entity }}" }`); on a project's page, those in the project; on a person's home, those in every project they read, which it must narrow to them with `{{ me }}`. A condition's value can be `{{ entity }}`, the entity whose page it is (on a tab), or `{{ me }}`, the person viewing it.

sort.description: The field they're in order of: one of the type's, or `hrid`, `created_at` or `updated_at`.

condition.description: A condition on a field (`field`, `op`, `value`), or a group of them (`all`, `any` or `not`), as the search API takes it.

field.description: A field of the type, or `hrid`, `created_by`, `created_at` or `updated_at`.

op.description: How `field` is compared with `value`: `eq`, `ne` or `in` (one of a list); `lt`, `lte`, `gt` or `gte`; `contains` or `starts_with` for a string, `contains` or `matches` for text; `has` for a list's item; `motif` for a sequence; `is_set` for any field. Each kind of field takes only some.

value.description: What to compare with, as the field takes it, or `{{ entity }}` or `{{ me }}`.

any.description: Conditions at least one of which must hold.
